text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Clouds over 1997 French economic growth forecasts. Certain forecasters revise predictions downwards; CDC sees GDP growth of around two percent.
-- Competition authorities impose fine of 20 million francs on France Telecom for "abuse of its monopoly" and fine of 10 million francs on Transpac, following complaint from British Telecom France.
-- U.S. job creation strength rekindles fears of overheating in the economy. Wall Street still counting on interest rate rise.
-- Luxury hotel owner group Monceau emerges from difficulties to keep its independence, Syrian businessman Osmane Aidi manages to hold on to management reins.
-- Airbus wins contracts worth 25 billion francs from Air Canada and Virgin.
